## 🎯 What is FraNchEstYN?

**FraNchEstYN** is a process-based framework for simulating and calibrating
crop–disease–fungicide dynamics. In five minutes you will:

1. Load the bundled Indiana dataset.
2. Configure crop and disease parameters.
3. Run a single calibration call.
4. Inspect the calibrated outputs.

The full case studies (Egypt, Ethiopia, Brazil, Indiana) show how to scale
this workflow to multi-site, multi-variety, and multi-season analyses.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4,
  message = FALSE, warning = FALSE
)
```

## 📦 Load the package

```{r libraries}
library(FraNchEstYN)
library(tidyverse)
library(kableExtra)
```

## 📥 Load bundled data

FraNchEstYN ships three Indiana datasets covering Septoria tritici blotch
observations (19 seasons, harvested 1973–1991) from Shaner & Buechley (1995):

```{r data}
data(weather_indiana)    # daily weather (NASA POWER)
data(reference_indiana)  # disease severity observations
data(management_indiana) # sowing and management metadata
```

```{r preview, echo=FALSE}
kable(
  weather_indiana %>% select(site, year, month, day, tx, tn, p, rad) %>% slice_head(n = 4),
  caption = "weather_indiana — first rows"
) %>% kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"))
```

## ⚙️ Set up parameters

Start from the built-in wheat and Septoria defaults. We disable parameters
unrelated to light interception and focus calibration on canopy and early
epidemic dynamics.

```{r parameters}
# --- Crop parameters: wheat defaults, enable only canopy-related calibration ---
thisCropParam <- cropParameters$wheat
thisCropParam <- set_calibration_flags(
  thisCropParam,
  disable = c("PartitioningMaximum", "TbaseCrop", "TmaxCrop", "ToptCrop",
              "FloweringStart", "RadiationUseEfficiency")
)

# --- Disease parameters: Septoria defaults, disable yield-loss pathways ---
thisDiseaseParam <- diseaseParameters$septoria
thisDiseaseParam <- set_calibration_flags(
  thisDiseaseParam,
  disable = c("RUEreducerDamage", "LightStealerDamage",
              "SenescenceAcceleratorDamage", "AssimilateSappersDamage")
)
```

## 🔧 Run the model

A single call to `franchestyn()` calibrates both the crop and disease
sub-models simultaneously. Here we use a short run (100 iterations) for
speed; increase to 500–1000 for publication-quality fits.

```{r calibration, eval=TRUE, results='hide'}
df <- franchestyn(
  weather_data      = weather_indiana,
  management_data   = management_indiana,
  reference_data    = reference_indiana,
  cropParameters    = thisCropParam,
  diseaseParameters = thisDiseaseParam,
  calibration       = "all",
  start_end         = c(1971, 1992),
  franchy_message   = FALSE,
  iterations        = 100
)
```

## 📊 Outputs

### Calibrated parameters

Calibrated values (🔴 red dot) vs default (🔵 blue line) and allowable
range (grey bar):

```{r param_plots, fig.height=5, fig.alt="Parameter ranges, default values and calibrated values for the Septoria disease parameters"}
df$diagnostics$calibration$plots$disease
```

### Performance metrics

```{r metrics, echo=FALSE}
df$diagnostics$metrics %>%
  filter(Variable == "DisSev") %>%
  select(GrowingSeason, n, Bias, RMSE, r, R2, NSE) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 3))) %>%
  kable(caption = "Calibration metrics — Disease Severity") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, font_size = 11,
                bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"))
```

### Season overview

Simulated (lines) vs observed (points) disease severity across all
simulated growing seasons:

```{r overview_plot, echo=FALSE, fig.height=6, fig.alt="Simulated and observed Septoria severity and canopy light interception for each growing season in Indiana"}
outputs <- df$outputs$simulation

ggplot(outputs, aes(x = as.Date(Date, format = "%m/%d/%Y"))) +
  geom_line(aes(y = LightIntHealthy, colour = "Healthy light int."),
            linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_line(aes(y = DiseaseSeverity, colour = "Disease severity"),
            linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(y = as.numeric(DiseaseSeverityRef), colour = "Observed severity"),
             shape = 21, size = 1.5, stroke = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~GrowingSeason, ncol = 6, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(
    name = NULL,
    values = c(
      "Healthy light int."  = "forestgreen",
      "Disease severity"    = "steelblue",
      "Observed severity"   = "steelblue"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "60 days", date_labels = "%b") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Proportion (0–1)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    strip.text       = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x      = element_text(size = 6, angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )
```
